title: Getting started with subnetr
text: connectome study measures functional connectivity every pair regions asks relates something subject: symptom score, drug dose, age. 100 regions 4,950 edges, testing one separately means paying multiplicity price leaves almost nothing standing. subnetr asks structured question instead. Rather “individual edges associated?”, asks “set regions whose mutual connections associated?” — subnetwork. usually scientific question anyway, far easier answer, subnetwork concentrates many weak edge-level signals one strong block-level signal.

title: Getting started with subnetr
text: Four steps, single function. edge_stats() turns subject-level connectivity one number per edge: evidence edge relates predictor, −log⁡10p-\log_{10} p scale, adjusted nuisance covariates. tune_subnet() chooses aggressively screen edges, search trade block size block density. subnet_extract() pulls dense blocks screened graph greedy peeling. subnet() 2–4 attaches permutation p-value block. practice call subnet() runs rest.

code: set.seed(42) n_subj  <- 120 n_nodes <- 60 n_edge  <- n_nodes * (n_nodes - 1) / 2  symptom <- rnorm(n_subj) age     <- rnorm(n_subj, 40, 12) motion  <- rexp(n_subj, 5)  fc <- matrix(rnorm(n_subj * n_edge), n_subj, n_edge) fc <- fc + outer(motion, rnorm(n_edge, sd = 0.4))   # a nuisance effect  W <- edge_stats(fc, x = symptom, covariates = cbind(age, motion)) dim(W) #> [1] 60 60 round(W[1:4, 1:4], 3) #>       [,1]  [,2]  [,3]  [,4] #> [1,] 0.000 0.277 0.300 0.140 #> [2,] 0.277 0.000 0.120 0.147 #> [3,] 0.300 0.120 0.000 0.698 #> [4,] 0.140 0.147 0.698 0.000 attr(W, "df") #> [1] 116 range(attr(W, "t")) #> [1] -3.238598  3.117976

title: subnetr 0.1.0
text: subnet() runs full pipeline: screen, tune, extract, test. subnet_extract() exposes greedy peeling . edge_stats() computes covariate-adjusted edge-wise association statistics subject-level connectivity, vectorized edges via Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem evaluated log p-value scale extreme evidence underflow. tune_subnet() selects screening threshold objective parameter. Reordered-matrix power-curve plots, plus membership(), dice(), vech() / unvech().
